title: Live call summarization — precision routing & quantization playbook
content:
Context and goal:

This is a working playbook for a customer POC: low-latency, high-accuracy live-call summarization for support centers (voice -> realtime transcript -> concise summary). The target is a mostly-automated pipeline that returns an actionable summary and intent tags to downstream ticketing in ~300ms median, with P95 under 800ms for typical 30s clip windows. The customer emphasizes: minimal hallucination on action items, speaker-aware summaries (agent vs. customer), and strict PII redaction before storage.

Primary constraints and success criteria:
- Latency SLOs: median first-summary token < 300ms after clip end; P95 < 800ms.
- Throughput: support 200 concurrent live calls with 1–4 summary requests per minute per call.
- Cost target: reduce hosted large-model tokens by >= 60% via cascade and caching relative to always-13B baseline.
- Quality: Extractive recall >= 0.85 (measured on human-labeled action items), abstractive summary fluency > 4.0/5 in spot checks, hallucination incidents < 1%.
- Privacy: PII redaction before any persisted embeddings; end-to-end encryption by default.

High-level architecture (pipeline sketch):
1) Audio ingestion -> streaming ASR (3rd-party or customer-provided). ASR emits partial transcripts + speaker diarization tokens.
2) Lightweight keyword/intent filter (on-edge tiny model or regex rules) to detect obvious non-summary cases (hold music, silent channels).
3) Small quantized model (2.7–6B quantized Q4/Q5) for fast extractive summary + confidence score. Produces: bullet points, extracted actions, confidence.
4) Router: if low confidence or long-turn complexity -> escalate to larger quantized model (13B Q4/GPTQ variant) in hosted tier for abstractive rewrite.
5) Post-process: PII scrubber, canonicalization, ticket creation payload, metadata logging (model used, tokens, latency).
6) Fallback: if top-tier model unavailable, return extractive summary with human-in-the-loop flag.

Why a cascade for this POC:
- Live summarization has tight tail-latency and high volume; always-serving large models is expensive.
- Many calls are routine and extractive summaries are sufficient; a cheap quantized model can handle the majority.
- Router enables balance between latency/cost and quality with clear observability.

Model selection rationale and candidates:
- Edge/tiny filter: Distil-RoBERTa intent classifier or 100M BiRNN fallback; inference must be < 5ms per transcript chunk.
- Fast extractive model: Llama 2 7B quantized (Q4_K_M / GPTQ) or a pruned 3B opt variant. Prioritize: low memory footprint, strong factual extraction.
- Abstractive quality model: 13B open model (Redwood-curated variant) compiled with kernels for NVidia A10/A100. Evaluate both 13B fp16 and 13B-GPTQ-4bit for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Safety/PII scrubber: rule-based pipeline + small NER model (fine-tuned) running before any downstream persistence.

Quantization strategy (practical plan):
- Start experiments with post-training GPTQ for 4-bit (gptq-pt) on the selected 13B and 7B checkpoints. Measure latency, perplexity delta, and extractive recall.
- For 7B fast model: target Q4_K_M or Q5 to reduce memory and keep KV cache friendly. Aim to fit in 8GB GPU l2 cache for shared-hosted pools.
- For 13B: attempt GPTQ-4 with outlier handling (per-channel clipping) + per-token dequant fallback for rare positions where accuracy drops.
- Evaluate dynamic precision routing: if a request has many numeric tokens (IDs, addresses) mark for higher-precision path.
- Document model artifacts (checksum + quantization recipe) and tie them to rollout tags in the console.

KV cache and prefix caching heuristics:
- Session-level KV cache for ongoing conversation (persisted in memory for up to 20 minutes idle) to avoid recomputing expensive context key-value pairs across successive summary requests.
- Prefix compression: canonicalize repeated system prompt material and store compressed pointers in cache to reduce token footprint.
- Cache invalidation: new topic detection (simple topic shift classifier) -> flush KV to avoid stale context leakage.

Prompt engineering & prompt pipeline:
- Minimal system prompt for extractive model: explicit instruction to: (1) list 3 action-items max, (2) tag urgency, (3) mark speaker attribution. Keep prompt <= 80 tokens.
- For abstractive rewrite: include structured placeholders: "[EXTRACTED_ACTIONS]", "[KEYPOINTS]", "[CUSTOMER_QUOTE]" to guide compression and reduce generation variance.
- Use constrained generation settings: max_new_tokens 120, temperature 0.0–0.2, top_p 0.8 for rewrite stage.
- Add safety tokens: post-generation NER pass and heuristic checks for hallucinated numbers/dates (if generation contains a 16-digit number or SSN-like pattern, route to human review).

Routing & fallback logic (decision tree):
- If extractive_confidence >= 0.9 -> return extractive summary (fast path).
- If confidence in [0.6,0.9) and tokens < 350 -> send to 13B-hosted rewrite for clarity.
- If confidence < 0.6 or extractive length > 6 bullets -> escalate.
- If hosted capacity saturated -> degrade to extractive summary + human-review flag and enqueue for async rewrite when capacity frees up.

Evaluation plan and metrics (POC):
- Offline dataset: 2k annotated transcripts (diverse acc regions), with labeled action items, gold abstractive summaries, and speaker tags.
- Real-time test harness: replay ASR stream with timing jitter and network emulation (packet loss, delay).
- Metrics:
  - Latency P50/P95/P99 for both extractive and abstractive flows.
  - Extractive recall/precision on action items.
  - Abstractive ROUGE-L and human Fluency/Hallucination score.
  - Cost: tokens and effective $/summary.
  - Failure modes: percent flagged for human review.

Experiment schedule (6-week POC sprint):
- Week 1: baseline measurements (always-13B hosted), gather dataset, small filter prototype.
- Week 2: quantize 7B candidate, benchmark locally (latency, extractive recall).
- Week 3: deploy 7B fast path in canary; A/B test against baseline on 20% traffic.
- Week 4: GPTQ-4x 13B variant rollout to second canary; run escalations and monitor quality deltas.
- Week 5: safety/PII integration, KV caching enabled for canary; stress test with 200 concurrent sessions.
- Week 6: compile results, cost analysis, and run executive demo.

Observability and instrumentation (what to log):
- Model selection event (model_id, quantization_recipe, tokens_consumed, latency_ms).
- Confidence scores and routing decisions.
- Token-level cost attribution and cumulative cost per call.
- Traces for ASR -> extract -> rewrite -> post-process with spans and error tags.
- Privacy audit logs for any PII redaction events.

Rollout and reliability controls:
- Canary percentages controlled by route policy in Redwood Console; automatic rollback on quality regression > 5% or latency SLO breach for 5m window.
- Circuit breaker: if hosted-13B average queue time > 200ms, switch to extractive-only route.
- Graceful degradation: include clear UI markers when summary is extractive-only and possibly incomplete.

Open questions / risks (items for customer workshop):
- ASR quality variability across accents: do we need to include accent-specific models or post-translation normalization?
- Regulatory limits on recording storage: customer mandates immediate ephemeral processing for EU calls — requires private-deploy variant.
- Is the customer willing to accept extractive-only summaries for some % of calls to meet cost targets?
- Human-in-the-loop SLA: acceptable turnaround for async rewrite requests?

Immediate action items (next 2 weeks):
- Annotate 500 representative transcripts (priority: complex calls, escalations) and hand-label action items. Owner: Ethan.
- Spike: GPTQ recipe trial for 13B candidate (Liam) — measure P95 latency on A10.
- Build replay harness with simulated jitter and mixed ASR error rates (Marisol).
- Draft canary rollout plan for Redwood Console with traffic % steps and automated health checks (Priya).

Appendix — quick checklist for experiments:
- [ ] Confirm ASR latency and transcript partials shape (word-per-sec distribution).
- [ ] Choose 7B and 13B checkpoints, store checksums.
- [ ] Run GPTQ-4 on training snapshots, keep unquantized reference for A/B.
- [ ] Implement confidence heuristics and logging schema.
- [ ] Add PII scrubber to pre-persist pipeline and test with synthetic PII cases.

Notes to self / workshop talking points:
- Emphasize tradeoff: many calls are solved cheaply — our cascade reduces cost without increasing human review burden.
- Show demo variations: fast extractive live view vs final abstractive ticket text.
- Prepare fallback SLAs and human-review UX (how tickets show "needs clarity").

End of doc — this remains a living draft. Update after first canary run with measured deltas and chosen quantization recipe.
